newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch hike special advances by 20 basis points.
newsitem.headline: Dutch hike special advances by 20 basis points.

text.p: The Dutch central bank raised its special advances rate on Thursday to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent for its new seven-day money market pact.
A central bank spokesman said the rate increase was in response to recent rises in Dutch money market rates.
"The market had expected this to some extent...market rates had already risen somewhat, and we are following that," he said.
The spokesman said the move was not prompted by recent guilder weakness against the German mark.
Most money market dealers had expected the special advances rate to rise, but some said the move was overdone. They said a 10-basis point increase would have been enough.

Asked why the bank had raised the special advances rate more than expected, the spokesman said "if you raise it by 10 (basis points), you might have to add another 10 later. So, you might as well make it 20."
The special advances rate usually sets the tone for money market rates.
The special advances rate, which had been pegged at 2.50 percent since last August, is roughly equivalent to Germany's repo rate and is the benchmark for all Dutch money market rates.
Germany's repo rate has been fixed at 3.00 percent since August.

The central bank spokesman said there would be no changes for now in the Dutch secured loans rate, roughly equivalent to Germany's discount rate. Commercial banks use the secured loans rate as a benchmark for their long-term loans to customers.
The secured loans rate has been pegged at 2.00 percent since April 1996.
Dutch money market dealers also did not expect the rate hike would to affect rates in the market much because a rate hike had been priced in.
One money market dealer said the move should also be seen in the light of the move towards European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"The guilder has to be brought closer towards parity with the German mark and the Dutch special advances has to move closer to the German repo," he said.
The gap between the Dutch special advances rate and the German repo rate narrowed to 30 basis points after the Dutch rate hike.
